title: Java inheritance problem
description: I don't understand how inheritance works in Java. Can someone explain it with an example?

replies.message: Inheritance allows one Java class to acquire the properties and methods of another class using the extends keyword.

Inheritance in Java is a feature where one class acquires the properties and methods of another class. It lets you reuse code and create a logical hierarchy between related objects.How It WorksSuperclass (Parent): The general class whose features are inherited.Subclass (Child): The specialized class that inherits from the parent using the extends keyword.extends keyword: Tells Java that the child class builds upon the parent class.

title: Python list problem
description: I don't understand how to remove duplicate elements from a Python list.

replies.message: You can remove duplicates from a Python list by converting it into a set, for example: list(set(my_list)).
The easiest way to remove duplicate elements from a Python list is by using the built-in set() function or dict.fromkeys() method.

title: How do I create a Python list?
description: I am learning Python and I don't understand how to create and use a list.

replies.message: A Python list can be created using square brackets. For example: my_list = [1, 2, 3, 4]

# Create an empty list empty_list = []  # A list of text (strings) fruits = ["apple", "banana", "cherry"]  # A list of numbers (integers) numbers = [10, 20, 30, 40]  # A mixed list mixed_list = [1, "hello", True, 3.14]

To create a Python list, you wrap your items inside square brackets [] and separate them with commas. [1] (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LWeS6R9IPf4&vl=en), [2] (https://www.w3schools.com/python/python_lists.asp)Lists are used to store multiple items in a single variable. They are highly flexible because they are ordered (they keep their sequence) and changeable (you can add or remove items later). title: linked list
description: i cant understand the single linked list

replies.message: A Singly Linked List is a fundamental linear data structure where elements are not stored in contiguous memory locations. Instead, each element is a separate object called a Node, and they are linked together using pointers.

title: double linked list
description: i cant understand the operations of double linked list

replies.message: A doubly linked list (DLL) is a data structure where each element (called a node) contains three parts: the actual data, a pointer to the next node, and an extra pointer to the previous node. This two-way connection allows you to traverse or navigate the list both forward and backward.
